title: Grateful Dead Live at Springfield Civic Center on 1972-10-02
lineage: Data DVD -> Adobe Audition v3.0 -> Samplitude Professional v11.2 -> FLAC
source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Dat -> Data DVD

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a high‑energy Fall ’72 show with smoking Bird Song, Cumberland Mines and a standout Playing in the Band.
ai_review.review: The recording is a crisp SBD tape that lets the band’s evolving mellow‑garage vibe shine through, even if the drum mix sits a bit low at times. Musically the concert is a firecracker – the first set “off the hook” with Bird Song, Cumberland Mines and a monster Playing in the Band, while the second set delivers solid jams (China→Rider transition) despite a few weaker moments like Tomorrow Is Forever. Overall it’s a highly enjoyable snapshot of the Dead’s mature 1972 sound.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high praise for both performance and sound quality across many detailed reviews; minor mix quirks do not detract from an overall excellent experience.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clear SBD capture with prominent keys and guitar; drums a bit recessed for some listeners; occasional mix balance notes but no major dropouts or noise.

standout_songs: Tomorrow Is Forever (duet) – noted for its novelty
poor_songs: Tomorrow Is Forever (some reviewers disliked it)
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set rolls on a tight, high‑energy groove with several epic jams; second set remains solid with extended explorations but has a few uneven spots toward the end.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for a fat, soaring tone, inventive noodling and strong solos (water‑wavy tones on PITB).
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for powerful bass lines that drive jams, solid backing vocals on Cumberland and strong presence in the China→Rider transition.
band_member_comments.Bob: Comments range from playful “out‑of‑tune” guitar texture to tight staccato chords and good interplay with Jerry during jams.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keys (Keith) praised for being forward in the mix; some reviewers note he’s a bit subdued but generally adds nice color, especially on transitions.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill's drumming is occasionally hard to hear in this Miller SBD, but overall rhythm section supports the high‑energy feel.
